motion: I THEREFORE MOVE that City Council INSTRUCT the Department of Neighborhood Empowerment, with assistance from the Los Angeles Fire Department (LAFD), to provide a report with recommendations to require the majority of all Neighborhood Council board members to obtain and maintain certification with LAFD’s CERT Program, including implementation options, timelines, costs, exemptions, and renewal requirements. The department should consider more accessible training opportunities, such as providing the CERT Program remotely. documents.excerpt: CITY OF LOS ANGELES BOARD OF NEIGHBORHOOD CALIFORNIA COMMISSIONERS LEONARD SHAFFER PRESIDENT 20th FLOOR, CITY HALL 200 NORTH SPRING STREET KEREN WATERS LOS ANGELES, CA 90012 VICE PRESIDENT TELEPHONE (213) 978-1551 TOLL-FREE 3-1-1 DEBBIE WEHBE E-MAIL: EmpowerLA@lacity.org GINA FIELDS FLOR CHAIDEZ CARMEN CHANG RANDELL ERVING GENERAL MANAGER DOUGLAS EPPERHART ERICK MUÑOZ KAREN BASS COMMISSION EXECUTIVE ASSISTANT Email: commission@empowerla.org MAYOR www.EmpowerLA.org November 2, 2026 Honorable Members of the Los Angeles City Council: SUBJECT:​ REPORT REGARDING COUNCIL FILE NO. 26-0906-S4 : Recommendations to Increase Neighborhood Council Board Member Voluntary Participation in Los Angeles Fire Department’s Community Emergency Response Team Program Executive Summary As amended on August 19, 2026, while no longer requiring Neighborhood Council Board Members to obtain and maintain Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) certification, Council File 26-0906-S4 directs the Department of Neighborhood Empowerment (the Department), to provide recommendations to increase Neighborhood Council Board Member engagement in the CERT program for Neighborhood Council Board Members with assistance from the Los Angeles Fire Department (LAFD). This matter follows the Lineage Fire in June 2026, prompting shelter-in-place orders, a 60-day emergency declaration from the Mayor of Los Angeles, widespread emergency response initiatives, and ongoing community, business, and environmental recovery efforts. The Lineage Fire and the City’s response to it underscores the critical value of neighborhood-level preparedness and coordination between City departments and community leaders. The CERT program and Neighborhood Council system share a community-based, volunteer-driven philosophy, yet serve distinct purposes. CERT focuses strictly on emergency preparedness and immediate disaster response, training thousands of volunteers annually. Neighborhood Councils ensure all Angelenos are represented in City government, meeting regularly as volunteer elected officials to discuss community issues, collaborate with their City Councilmember and other City departments, and hear insights and input from community members. Neighborhood Councils advocate for their community on issues including emergency preparation and disaster response, as well as land use, housing, social services, public transportation, and many others. The principal policy issue is how the City can make the 17.5 hours of in-person CERT training more accessible to Board Members. Board Members are volunteer elected officials who are already required to complete at least five hours of mandatory City governance training before they are able to represent their community at committee meetings, board meetings, events, and other community and civic engagement initiatives.
